newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries end mostly down, profits booked late.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries end mostly down, profits booked late.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries ended flat to modestly lower on Thursday, as late session profit-taking erased gains made earlier in the day.
The 30-year bond closed down 4/32 at 101-25/32, while its yield rose to 6.49 percent from 6.48 percent.
"I have got to believe that we are close to the top," said Vincent Verterano, head trader at Nomura Securities. "The market is difficult and it will probably stay that way the next couple months."
Treasuries moved higher from the start, shrugging off a slew of mainly strong economic news, on a wave of retail and hedge fund buying.
Later in the session, continued money from mortgage-backed securities into Treasuries aided the market's positive tone.
Activity was described as volatile, with plenty of willing sellers as well as buyers. Yet, the bulk of action was seen in the morning.
According to GovPX, volume was roughly $75 billion at 1500 EDT/1900 GMT.
With the market coming off a near one-point gain on Tuesday, momentum pushed Treasuries up early this session.
The market's ascent paused after the Labor Department reported a drop in initial jobless claims last week to 349,000 from 377,000 the prior week.

Meanwhile, housing starts rose to a 1.45 million annual unit rate in June, from May's 1.385 million, and the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia's business outlook survey's main index rose to 28.1 in July from 25.2 in June.
"The news was strong today," said one senior trader at a large U.S. bank.
Yet, the market largely shrugged off the numbers, instead concentrating on technical factors such as flows.
Traders reported central bank buying at the front end, Middle East account buying in two-year notes and buying in 10-year notes after one account sold a block of mortgage backed securities.

Then, reports of Speaker of the House Newt Gingrich signing up 95 House members in introducing a bill requiring budget surpluses to pay down the national debt pushed Treasuries to session highs, with the 30-year bond up as close to a half-point at one point.

Market participants figured the Treasuries would end the day with solid gains, but profit-taking and the failure for the September bond contract to hold above 114-26/32 sent the market lower just before the futures close.

In late trading, the two-year note was unchaged at 100-8/32 to yield 5.86 percent, the five-year fell 2/32 to 100-19/32 to yield 6.11 percent, and the 10-year note was down 1/32 at 103-4/32, yielding 6.19 percent.

The three-month bill was up three basis points at a discount rate of 5.08 percent, the six-month was up two basis points at 5.11 percent and the one-year bill was down one basis point at 5.22 percent.
